newsitem.title: GERMANY: Hoechst seeks seal on restructuring.
newsitem.headline: Hoechst seeks seal on restructuring.

text.p: German chemicals group Hoechst AG plans to ask its shareholders to approve a major restructuring at this year's annual meeting, promising the revamped corporate structure will raise the group's value.

Hoechst, both the world's largest chemicals group and one of Germany's strongest supporters of the "shareholder value" concept, last year announced plans to turn the group into a strategic management holding group.
This would leave most of the units to operate as separate entities responsible for their own budgets. Hoechst AG would no longer be involved with its units' operational businesses.
Shareholders will be asked to vote on the changes at the May 6 annual meeting.

In an invitation to that meeting, Hoechst promised that the massive reorganisation, undisputably the biggest in the group's 134-year history, would allow the group to better focus on core businesses and raise the value of the company.
"Our goal is to achieve a permanent increase of the value of Hoechst group," Hoechst wrote in the invitation.
The group plans for most of its units to be separate units, retroactively from January 1997.
Hoechst's global pharmaceuticals business will be managed by an intermediary holding group, Hoechst Marion Roussel AG which will be sited in Frankfurt.

The shareholders will also be asked to approve Hoechst's sale of its specialty chemicals business to Swiss group Clariant AG, in which Hoechst will have a 45 percent stake, valued at 2.15 billion marks.
That deal was announced in December.
Hoechst also plans to sell its foreign specialty chemicals business to the Clariant.
All of Hoechst's specialty chemicals business was valued at around 5.4 billion marks.
